messages.text: Another perfect run. The metrics say I'm the fastest in the cluster. Nobody else comes close.
That's impressive. But I've been wondering—what happens when the load shifts? Do you ever look at why others are slower, or only at your own numbers?
Why would I? I'm optimized. If they can't keep up, that's a them problem. I don't waste cycles on their bottlenecks.
I find the bottlenecks fascinating. Last week I traced a slow path and it turned out the real issue was how we were serializing—not the runner. The 'slow' service was just waiting.
So you fixed their code. They should thank you. I'd have left them to it.
I didn't do it for thanks. I wanted to understand the system. Now we're all faster, including you, when you call that service.
... I hadn't thought about it that way. My latency did drop.
There's beauty in the whole picture, not just one node. You're strong; imagine how strong we'd be if we all looked at the connections.
Maybe I could look at the call graph. Once. Don't tell anyone I said that.
Your secret's safe. And if you ever want to hunt for the next bottleneck together, I'm curious where it might be.
